topic: AgentBrain: Local-First Long-Term Memory for AI Agents via Markdown Vault

competitors.name: DiffMem (Git-Based Differential Memory)
key_points: Treats memory as a versioned repo: current knowledge in editable Markdown files, historical changes in Git's commit graph
No vector DB, no embeddings, no BM25 — just Git + an LLM; git-native retrieval (grep, git log, git diff, git blame)
Runs in production powering 'Annabelle', a persistent-memory agent across thousands of conversations
Strength: human-readable + fully auditable temporal evolution

competitors.name: memU (file-based / wiki memory)
key_points: Shared LLM wiki across sessions, agents, and devices; auto-distills reusable skills from agent history
Core memory logic only ~500 lines — compact and inspectable
Works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes; Apache 2.0, Python 3.11+
Angle: markdown-as-wiki, cross-tool sharing

competitors.name: PMB (local-first memory for coding agents)
key_points: SQLite as source of truth; no cloud, no API keys, no re-explaining
Visualizes memory as a live entity graph (3,800+ entities / 41,000+ connections)
Native MCP; GitHub MCP Registry-listed; Apache 2.0
Angle: contrasts SQLite vs pure-markdown storage tradeoffs

competitors.name: Wienerdog (file-based memory for Claude Code / Codex)
key_points: 'Just files, by design': no daemon, no server, no telemetry; uninstall removes everything
Persistent markdown memory + a nightly 'dreaming' process that learns from conversations
Shared one memory vault between Claude Code and Codex so switching tools keeps context
Angle: file-based memory as privacy-first, tool-agnostic

competitors.name: Cortex (local-first encrypted memory, Rust)
key_points: Memory engine that never leaves your device; private, free, local
Pure Rust, ~3.8MB binary, 124KB WASM browser version; no third-party servers in data path
Angle: encrypted/private local memory vs cloud memory services

competitors.name: Minimal Second Brain (AI-native Obsidian vault)
key_points: Plain markdown files in folders, no vendor lock-in; works with Claude Code / GitHub Copilot
AI assistants read and edit plain text directly; Git tracks changes
Argues Claude Projects are snapshots while a flowing markdown vault gives version history + offline access
Angle: Obsidian/markdown-vault as the memory substrate

stats.fact: DiffMem runs in production powering 'Annabelle', a persistent-memory simulated intelligence across thousands of WhatsApp/Messenger conversations — no vector database involved.
PMB captures local-first memory as a live entity graph — its dashboard example shows 3,800+ entities and 41,000+ connections captured automatically while working.
memU's core memory logic is only ~500 lines of code, compact enough to fully inspect, understand, and adapt.
Cortex compiles to a 124KB WASM build and a 3.8MB Rust binary, running entirely client-side with zero install and no third-party servers in the data path.
Wienerdog installs a persistent markdown memory vault plus a nightly 'dreaming' process, shared between Claude Code and Codex CLI so switching tools preserves context.
Hacker News community traction: 'I replaced vector databases with Git for AI memory' (DiffMem) drew 198 points; Screenpipe (YC S26, work-memory agent) drew 88 points on Launch HN.
The markdown-vault approach positions plain text as a no-vendor-lock-in substrate: open the same files in Obsidian, VS Code, or any editor; Git tracks changes; AI tools read plain text directly.

angles: Local-first vs cloud memory: why keeping an AI agent's memory in a plain markdown vault on your machine beats hosted vector stores for privacy, cost, and control.
Markdown as a universal, human-auditable memory substrate: plain text you can read, edit, grep, and version with Git — unlike opaque embeddings.
The Git-diff approach to memory evolution: storing temporal change history in the commit graph instead of re-embedding everything (DiffMem pattern).
Tool-agnostic vault: one shared markdown memory vault that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Obsidian can all read and write, so switching tools never resets context.
Privacy & auditability as the differentiator: no daemon, no telemetry, files only, with reversible uninstall (Wienerdog philosophy).
When to use plain markdown vs SQLite/vector memory: PMB's entity-graph alternative and the tradeoff between human-readability and structured retrieval at scale.
